note: guard() is pure and deterministic, so it is exactly the kind of thing that must not differ by language. Expectations are the sorted list of FAILED check keys - messages are prose and stay free. The pii:* kinds come from fixtures/pii.json, which crates/anon exports.

guard.name: iso-dates-are-not-phone-numbers
guard.why: The regression this whole item exists for. The SDKs shipped `(?:\+?\d[\s().-]?){10,}`, which matches every ISO date; the server replaced it in D14 and the SDKs did not follow. A changelog entry is not PII.
guard.output: The incident began on 2026-07-01 and was closed on 2026-07-03.

guard.name: version-strings-are-not-phone-numbers
guard.why: Same pre-D14 rule ate `1.2.3-4.5.6`. Release notes are the single most common thing an LLM is asked to summarise.
guard.output: Upgrade to version 1.2.3-4.5.6 before Friday; 10.14.2 is end of life.

guard.name: short-digit-groups-are-not-phone-numbers
guard.why: Under-matching is the deliberate bias: an order number is not a phone number.

guard.name: email-is-pii
guard.output: Reach me at alice.smith+tag@example.co.uk any time.

guard.name: international-phone-is-pii
guard.output: Call the on-call at +1 415 555 2671 if it pages.

guard.name: api-key-is-pii
guard.why: The scrubber redacts secrets; a guard that let a model echo one back into a response would be strictly weaker than the ingest path it fronts.

guard.name: several-kinds-report-once-each
guard.why: Kinds are families - three phone shapes are one finding. A caller wants to know a phone number leaked, not which of three regexes noticed.
guard.output: Mail bob@x.io, or the box at 10.0.0.1, or +44 20 7946 0958.

guard.name: json-key-missing
guard.why: Locks the `key:<name>` check-key spelling across languages.

guard.name: too-many-words
guard.why: Locks the snake_case check keys. The TypeScript SDK used maxWords/minWords/maxChars/mustMatch/noPII while Python and Rust used snake_case, so the same verdict was not the same value.

guard.name: pattern-rules-violated
guard.why: Locks `not_match:<pattern>` on the raw pattern text. TypeScript keyed it on the stringified RegExp (`/nope/`), which no other language could produce.
